page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud instance based on x86_64 architecture and managed via KVM hypervisor technology. The system features 128 dedicated vCPUs provided by Intel Xeon 8369B processors running at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It includes 1024 GB of system memory, establishing a high memory density with an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU). The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU hardware accelerators.

Network performance is supported by a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. A key architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage, requiring all persistent data operations to rely on remote block storage solutions over the high-speed network interface. From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the substantial RAM allocation per core permits the consolidation of large memory-bound applications into a single instance, reducing multi-node clustering complexity and resource overhead.

Given its hardware specifications, ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge is structured for memory-demanding enterprise workloads. Primary application fits include large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis, enterprise resource planning systems, real-time analytics, and heavy data processing frameworks requiring massive memory buffers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr7.32xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 128 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8369B processors operating at 2.9 GHz on x86_64 architecture. Equipped with 1024 GB of system RAM, it maintains an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per core), delivering high memory density for enterprise-scale workloads. The instance operates without discrete local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on a 64 Gbps baseline network bandwidth for external storage and interconnect traffic. While the absence of local disks necessitates network-attached storage for persistent data, the substantial memory capacity offers strong qualitative cost efficiency by consolidating large in-memory databases and analytics engines on a single node. This configuration fits high-capacity enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, large-scale Redis caching, enterprise resource planning systems, and real-time data processing platforms.
